data.narrative:
Deep Isolation, a Series A nuclear energy company founded by Elizabeth Muller and Richard A. Muller, is evaluated within a fragmented sector comp universe of 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, and General Matter. The company has raised $26M to date.

Given the scarcity of same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within nuclear energy, peer-median triangulation was not applicable; fewer than 3 datapoints survived filtering for stage, sector, and valuation tier. Stage-progression methodology was therefore the primary analytical lever. Using $26M in total raised as a baseline valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-Series B advancement, this method implies a valuation of $52M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $44M to $60M, centered on $52M. This range reflects uncertainty bands around the single applicable method rather than consensus across multiple triangulation approaches. Key unknowns include the absence of direct peer-trading multiples in this early-stage nuclear segment and whether Deep Isolation's technology positioning commands a premium or discount to the broader frontier-energy cohort. Sensitivity to the stage-progression multiplier itself—whether nearer 1.7x or 2.3x—drives material movement within the band.
